title: Cache Stampede
subtitle: Mitigating dogpiling and thundering herds using Singleflight Request Coalescing, Distributed Leases, and Probabilistic Early Expiration (XFetch).
keyTakeaways: A Cache Stampede (Dogpiling) happens when a popular cached key expires and thousands of concurrent requests simultaneously miss the cache and hammer the database with identical expensive queries.

Request Coalescing (`Singleflight` in Go) deduplicates concurrent in-flight cache misses within an application node so only 1 request queries the DB/cache and shares the result with all waiting callers.
Probabilistic Early Expiration (PER / XFetch) recomputes hot keys asynchronously *before* their TTL expires based on recomputation time and remaining TTL.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: When a cached homepage payload or expensive aggregation expires under 10,000 RPS, and the DB query takes 200ms, 2,000 requests will see a cache miss during that 200ms window and launch 2,000 duplicate DB queries. You can eliminate this in two layers: per-process Singleflight and cross-process Distributed Leases.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: A Cache Stampede (Dogpiling) happens when a popular cached key expires and thousands of concurrent requests simultaneously miss the cache and hammer the database with identical expensive queries.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: Request Coalescing (`Singleflight` in Go) deduplicates concurrent in-flight cache misses within an application node so only 1 request queries the DB/cache and shares the result with all waiting callers.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Cache Stampede:
bullets: **In-Process Singleflight + Distributed Lease Lock**: Provides strictly caps database load to 1 query across the entire cluster even on a completely cold cache. Best suited for Expensive DB queries, cold-cache startups, and API gateway aggregation layers.

**Soft TTL / Probabilistic Early Expiration (XFetch)**: Provides zero tail-latency spike for users because refreshes happen before hard expiration. Best suited for High-QPS feeds, homepage modules, and low-latency p99 SLA services.

In-Process Request Coalescing (`Singleflight`): Maintain an in-memory map of `inflightPromises: Map<string, Promise<T>>`. If `key` is already being fetched on this pod, subsequent callers simply `await` the existing Promise. If you have 20 pods, max DB queries drop from 2,000 to at most 20.

Distributed Lease / Mutex (`SET lock:key 1 NX PX 2000`): Out of those 20 pods, only the 1 pod that acquires the Redis lock queries the database; the other 19 either serve slightly stale data (Soft TTL) or wait briefly for the cache to be populated.
Zero Lock Coordination Needed: XFetch works purely from local math on each cache hit without extra Redis lock round-trips.
Self-Tuning by Popularity: The higher the QPS on a key, the more trials per second, guaranteeing an early refresh exclusively for genuinely hot keys.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Cache Stampede across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Expensive DB queries, cold-cache startups, and API gateway aggregation layers, suited for environments requiring Strictly caps database load to 1 query across the entire cluster even on a completely cold cache.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for High-QPS feeds, homepage modules, and low-latency p99 SLA services, where Zero tail-latency spike for users because refreshes happen before hard expiration.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Instead of waiting for a hot key to hard-expire and then scrambling to coordinate locks, the XFetch algorithm (published in VLDB 2015) stores the recomputation duration (`delta`) alongside the cached item. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Cache Stampede introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: callers on a completely cold key must wait for the winner to finish querying the db.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: only prevents stampedes on already-cached hot keys; still needs singleflight for initial cold misses.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Cache Stampede:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Probabilistic Early Expiration (PER / XFetch) recomputes hot keys asynchronously *before* their TTL expires based on recomputation time and remaining TTL.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Combine both techniques in your answer: 'I will use Soft TTL / Probabilistic Early Refresh so hot keys refresh in the background before expiring, and Singleflight request coalescing to protect against cold-start misses.'
